title: The Six Shooter
paragraphs: Adult western drama starring James Stewart as Britt Ponset. The GRH container includes the July 1953 sales audition, all 39 regular NBC episodes, one exact duplicate collection copy of episode 30, and three short editorial/reference tracks; the April 1952 Hollywood Star Playhouse precursor is documented historically but is not preserved here as a full broadcast object.
GRH documents the program through NBC regular run (September 20, 1953 to June 24, 1954) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Basil Adlam (music on 41 recordings, composer on 3 recordings, conductor on 3 recordings, and music director on 1 recording), Jack Johnstone (director on 41 recordings, performer on 1 recording, producer on 1 recording, and production supervisor on 1 recording), James Stewart (performer on 41 recordings), Jimmy Stewart (performer on 39 recordings), Frank Burt (creator on 37 recordings and writer on 33 recordings), Hal Gibney (announcer on 20 recordings and host on 1 recording), and John Wald (announcer on 17 recordings).

The program is also connected in the archive to [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] (broadcast on network) and [[org|org.cd82fd99edb39caa|Armed Forces Radio and Television Service]] (rebroadcast by).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include frontier western setting and culture, wandering gunfighter and outsider protagonist, frontier justice, law and moral choice, family loyalty and kinship, robbery, outlaw crime and pursuit, and revenge and cycles of violence.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Hollywood Star Playhouse precursor to a regular series, Adult western drama in late network radio, James Stewart film-western persona carried into radio, and Brief commercial sponsorship followed by sustaining broadcasts.

Programs with especially strong personnel connections in the GRH knowledge graph include [[show|yours-truly-johnny-dollar|Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar]] (49 shared credited people), [[show|lux-radio-theatre|Lux Radio Theatre]] (38 shared credited people), [[show|broadway-is-my-beat|Broadway Is My Beat]] (31 shared credited people), [[show|escape|Escape]] (31 shared credited people), and [[show|the-railroad-hour|The Railroad Hour]] (30 shared credited people).
